sources.title: GPT-5.1: A smarter, more conversational ChatGPT
sources.evidence: Dated November 12, 2025. Explicitly begins public ChatGPT rollout of GPT-5.1 Instant that day and identifies its forthcoming API name as gpt-5.1-chat-latest. Describes Instant adaptive reasoning and states that both API variants will have adaptive reasoning. The original Instant release is distinct from the Thinking model and router. Reopened October 27, 2026: no nominal total or active parameter size is stated; the release-family relationship does not supply a count.

sources.title: GPT-5.1 Chat API model documentation
sources.evidence: Directly fetched complete current Markdown. Exact alias has 128,000 context, text/image inputs, text output, 16,384 maximum output, function calling and Responses/Chat Completions support. It also lists a contradictory 272,000 maximum-input budget. No reasoning_tokens or prompt_caching feature flags are listed; cached-input pricing is present. Only the mutable alias is listed as a snapshot. Marked shut down. Rechecked October 27, 2026 using the official documentation fetch and freshly downloaded full Markdown: no total or active model-parameter count is listed.

sources.title: OpenAI API changelog
sources.evidence: Directly fetched changelog. November 13, 2025 release entry explicitly includes gpt-5.1-chat-latest among its model labels. This is the later API milestone, not the first ChatGPT Instant rollout. The separate same-day extended-cache announcement explains storage of key/value tensors. Default none reasoning language concerns gpt-5.1, so is not transferred to this chat alias.

sources.title: GPT-5.1 Instant and GPT-5.1 Thinking System Card Addendum
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026 and read the complete original five-page PDF. The introduction distinguishes GPT-5.1 Instant, Thinking and Auto routing; Tables 1-3 contain safety and image-input metrics. No nominal total or active parameter count is given.

sources.title: Prompt caching
sources.evidence: Directly fetched current guide. Its explicit extended-retention model list includes gpt-5.1-chat-latest, separately from gpt-5.1 and Codex variants. Describes cached key/value tensors and distinguishes pre-GPT-5.6 behavior. This provides exact-model caching support beyond cached pricing alone.

sources.title: Prompt Caching 201
sources.evidence: Directly fetched guide expressly applies to pre-GPT-5.6 models. Explains prompt caching using Transformer attention-layer key/value projections and cached tensors across layers/heads. Joined with the exact chat-alias support list, supports a limited operational Transformer inference rather than a complete block specification.

sources.title: File inputs
sources.evidence: Directly fetched guide. Responses processes PDF text and page images for vision-capable models; Chat Completions accepts PDF file content parts. Joined to exact alias image-input and endpoint support, establishes PDF as an API file format rather than a distinct native model modality.

sources.title: API deprecations
sources.evidence: Directly fetched April 22, 2026 notice explicitly records access to gpt-5.1-chat-latest shut down on July 23, 2026. This agrees with the current model page status; no endpoint call was attempted.

sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
sources.evidence: Current section 9.1 reserves service intellectual-property rights and grants limited service access. Supports a descriptive proprietary classification of this hosted model, not an open-weight license or a statement that the same contract wording applied at launch.

sources.title: All OpenAI API models
sources.evidence: Directly fetched catalog lists GPT-5.1 Chat as a shut-down hosted model, separately from the explicitly open-weight Apache-2.0 gpt-oss section. No downloadable GPT-5.1 Chat weights are offered in these sources.

sources.title: Update to GPT-5 System Card: GPT-5.2
sources.evidence: Rechecked October 27, 2026 using the freshly downloaded full original PDF text. GPT-5.1 Instant appears in safety, jailbreak, prompt-injection, vision and health comparisons. The model-training section and comparison tables supply no nominal total or active parameter count for Instant. Comparisons use later versions of earlier models; GPT-5.2 descriptions do not establish GPT-5.1 size.

sources.title: GPT-5.5 Instant System Card
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026 and inspected the fresh original PDF text, including training and exact gpt-5.1-instant comparison tables. Tables 1-5 report safety, vision, mental-health, prompt-injection and HealthBench metrics, without a total or active parameter-size column. The card cautions that earlier-model comparisons use latest versions; no nominal GPT-5.1 Instant count is disclosed.

sources.title: Introducing GPT-5.1 for developers
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The November 13 developer announcement lists gpt-5.1-chat-latest alongside gpt-5.1 in availability; its appendix evaluates GPT-5.1 (high), not the Instant alias. Adaptive reasoning, price and benchmark scores provide no nominal total or active parameter count and are not used to transfer size from the separate Thinking variant.

sources.title: GPT-5.3 Instant System Card
sources.evidence: Opened October 27, 2026 and read the complete freshly downloaded five-page PDF. Section 2 describes training data and notes that earlier-model comparisons use updated versions. Tables 1-2 explicitly include gpt-5.1-instant but contain safety and mental-health scores, without total or active parameter counts. This later original model-team comparison adds no supported size disclosure.

name.note: Exact official API display name; the original launch binds this API alias to GPT-5.1 Instant.

developer.note: First-party announcement and model documentation identify the developer.

family.note: The chat/Instant variant belongs to the GPT-5.1 release family, an iteration within the broader GPT-5 generation.

release_date.note: Earliest public release of the explicitly bound Instant model is November 12 in ChatGPT. API alias availability follows November 13; the API specifications below do not claim ChatGPT had identical interface limits at launch.

open_weights.note: Documented distribution is hosted ChatGPT/API service access under reserved service IP. Publisher separately identifies its open-weight models; no weights for this exact model are offered in the reviewed primary material.

license.note: Descriptive service/model classification, not a named downloadable-weight license or launch-date contract reconstruction.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 review found no published nominal total for the exact Instant/chat alias in the original release, API specification or system card, or the later GPT-5.2, GPT-5.3 Instant and GPT-5.5 Instant comparisons. Separate targeted searches for total parameters, billion counts and later research/model-team tables found no supported exact-model disclosure or named counted-base lineage. Generic GPT-5.1 estimates and the separate Thinking model do not establish this value.

active_parameters_b.note: Rechecked separately on October 27. No active/activated count is stated for GPT-5.1 Instant in the original specifications or later exact-model comparisons; those tables report evaluation scores. Searches using the Instant name and exact API alias with active parameters, Activated Params and research-table terms found no supported nominal active-count convention. Adaptive reasoning describes deliberation, not an activated-parameter count; no dense-equality or sibling transfer is applied.

architecture.note: Qualified cross-source operational inference: the caching guide explicitly names gpt-5.1-chat-latest as supporting extended retention, and the applicable pre-GPT-5.6 technical explanation describes Transformer attention KV projections. This does not establish the complete block inventory, exclusively Transformer layers, dense/MoE routing, dimensions, or parameter counts. Exact model Markdown lacks a caching feature flag; its cached pricing is only corroborating evidence.

context_window.note: Both HTML and Markdown exact model pages explicitly label 128,000 as the context window, separately from 16,384 maximum output. Markdown also lists 272,000 maximum input, which conflicts with the context figure; that unresolved documentation inconsistency is preserved rather than used to inflate context. No endpoint test was made.

modalities.note: Native inputs are text and image, output is text. PDF denotes API extraction into text/page images for this vision-capable Responses/Chat Completions model. Hosted image-generation tools do not establish native image output.

reasoning.note: Original launch and system card explicitly describe Instant adaptive reasoning; the launch binds Instant to this exact chat API alias and states both upcoming API variants have adaptive reasoning. The current API page omits a reasoning_tokens flag, which does not negate the explicit model capability. No configurable reasoning-effort levels are asserted for this alias.

tool_call.note: Exact current Markdown and HTML explicitly support function calling. This is documented historical capability of a now-shut-down API alias.

description.value: GPT-5.1 Instant chat model with adaptive reasoning, text and image input, text output, and function calling in the API.
description.note: Replaces promotional assistant-positioning prose with documented variant and capabilities; distinguishes Instant from GPT-5.1 Thinking.

Update to GPT-5 System Card: GPT-5.2

patch.notes: GPT-5.1 Instant began public ChatGPT rollout on November 12, 2025; its gpt-5.1-chat-latest API alias followed on November 13. API specifications refer to the documented alias, whose final immutable target is not published on the model page. The 128,000-token context and 16,384-token output limit are explicit in HTML and Markdown; Markdown also lists an inconsistent 272,000 maximum-input budget, left unresolved. Adaptive reasoning is explicitly documented for Instant and its API binding, although the current model page has no reasoning_tokens flag; configurable effort controls are not asserted. PDF is an API file format processed into text/page images. Transformer is a qualified operational inference from exact-alias caching support and the pre-GPT-5.6 KV-attention explanation, not a complete architecture, dense/MoE classification or parameter disclosure. No nominal total or active parameter count is published in the reviewed exact-model specifications or later GPT-5.2, GPT-5.3 Instant and GPT-5.5 Instant comparison tables; both remain undisclosed. API access shut down July 23, 2026; no endpoint test was made.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit: freshly reopened the exact GPT-5.1 Instant/chat specification, original release and system card, developer launch and later GPT-5.2/GPT-5.3 Instant/GPT-5.5 Instant model-team comparisons. Independent total and active searches found no supported nominal counts or counted-base lineage; both remain explicitly null/undisclosed. Preserved all twelve unrelated field assessments.
